**Kill criteria:**
- Two consecutive quarters of YoY PAT decline.
- Order book below ₹8,000 cr.
- Debtor days above 120.
- Borrowings back above ₹1,000 cr without a matching order-book rise.
- Any promoter pledge.

`case_study:booking-priceline-2002-2025` · tickers US-BKNG · confidence: verified

Priceline fell from ~$974 (1999, adjusted for the 2003 1:6 reverse split) to ~$6.60-7 in Oct 2002 (-99%). CEO Jeffery Boyd and team bought UK Active Hotels (2004) and Dutch Booking.com (2005, ~$133m [unverified]); Booking.com's agency model (hotels pay commission after stay, broad SME hotel supply in Europe) became the profit engine. Fortune (2017): best total shareholder return of any large company over the prior decade; ~3,000% in 10 years to 2015. Reached ~$1,500+ by 2016-17 and ~$5,000-5,800 by 2025 [unverified]: roughly 800x from the 2002 low. Split: mostly EPS growth (gross bookings compounding 20-30% for a decade plus margin expansion and buybacks); P/E stayed ~20-30x [unverified]. Drawdowns: -99% 2000-02; ~-70% 2008 [unverified]; ~-45% 2020 COVID. EARLY SIGNAL visible 2005-07: international gross bookings growing far faster than the US name-your-own-price business and becoming the majority of profit, disclosed in segment data — while the market still saw a damaged US dot-com. Who caught it: few documented names; it was a classic 'hidden segment' that analysts initially underweighted. Stall: post-2018 growth normalised to ~10%, still compounding via buybacks. LESSON: a small acquired segment with platform economics inside an unloved parent can carry the whole valuation; read the segment notes.

- **Start → end:** ~$6.60 (Oct 2002, reverse-split adj) → ~$5,000-5,800 (2025) [unverified] (~800x)
- **EPS vs rerating:** mostly EPS + buybacks
- **Max drawdown:** -99% (2000-02); ~-70% 2008 [unverified]
- **Early signal:** Booking.com/Active Hotels international bookings growth in segment data
- **Who caught it:** not well documented
- **Ended/stalled:** growth normalised post-2018; still compounding
- **Lesson:** hidden segment with platform economics inside a broken parent
- **Sources:** [1](https://www.fool.com/investing/2017/09/18/could-the-priceline-group-inc-be-a-millionaire-mak.aspx) · [2](https://fortune.com/2014/02/06/booking-returns-on-priceline/) · [3](https://money.cnn.com/2015/08/05/investing/priceline-earnings-stock) · [4](https://www.foxbusiness.com/markets/priceline-stock-history-how-the-internet-travel-giant-became-a-blockbuster-stock)
